name: Hearing the scriptures (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Study of scripture and its right interpretation under a teacher. In Dvaita: hearing the true scriptures (Vedas, Mahābhārata, Pañcarātra, Purāṇas) with Madhva's commentaries so as to know Viṣṇu's supremacy, the five differences and gradation; the first principal means to knowledge, never to be curtailed.
stage: all (the lowest adhikārin qualifies by study and devotion)

name: Reflection (manana)
method_summary: Reasoned reflection on what has been heard, removing doubts and contrary views — in Dvaita often in the company of fellow students and through the tradition's disputations.

name: Meditation (nididhyāsana / dhyāna)
method_summary: Sustained meditation on the Lord. In Dvaita: meditation on Viṣṇu with the qualities suited to one's fitness, within one's heart as the original (bimba) of one's self; it is an independent means (not a subsidiary of hearing) and yields the direct realization that pleases the Lord.
signs_of_progress: direct realization (aparokṣa) of the Lord, within the scope one's fitness allows

warnings.text: One who strives for a vision he is unfit for falls even from what he had.

name: Worship of Hari with qualities according to fitness
method_summary: Meditative worship (upāsanā) of Hari under the qualities fit for the worshipper: Brahmā with all qualities, humans as bliss (ānanda), knower (jña) and the ever-existing Self (sadātmā); the gods are liberated when Hari becomes directly perceived through such worship.

warnings.text: A person who desires what he is unfit for surely falls; serve Viṣṇu according to your fitness.

name: Contemplation of oneself as the reflection of Nārāyaṇa
method_summary: Seated upright during the purifications before worship, one contemplates Nārāyaṇa in the lotus of the heart and one's own self before him as his reflection, and prays: 'You are the original, I am the reflection, though there is a difference between us; flawless Lord, separate my faults from me.'
signs_of_progress: removal of sin, according to the text
notes: A step within daily worship rather than a free-standing meditation; ritual details omitted.

name: Remembering Hari as the doer; action as worship
method_summary: Doing the prescribed duties and avoiding the forbidden, without desire for results, while remembering that Hari within moves one's limbs and that all acts of mind, speech and body are his worship — the Yogadīpikā's definition of yoga.

name: Ekādaśī fast
method_summary: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day of both fortnights as the 'vow of Nārāyaṇa's day', with rules for days overlapped by the tenth (fast on the twelfth instead) and for the time of breaking the fast. A one-day fast, not a prolonged one.
duration: one lunar day, broken on the following day
notes: The texts' own exemptions (for the sick, aged, etc.) were not checked; no warnings recorded.

name: Kṛṣṇa-Jayantī fast
method_summary: Fasting on Kṛṣṇa's birthday — the dark eighth day conjoined with Rohiṇī at midnight — to be kept by all, especially the twice-born and Hari's devotees.

name: Worship of Viṣṇu according to the Tantrasārasaṅgraha and Yogadīpikā
method_summary: Daily and occasional worship of Viṣṇu (and his forms, especially Kṛṣṇa, Narasiṃha and Rāma) with mantras derived from the praṇava, placing of letters and forms on the body, purifications, invocation into the image and offerings, remembering that Hari in the worshipper and Hari in the image is the one Lord who accepts the worship.

name: Placing the letters and forms of Viṣṇu (nyāsa)
method_summary: Placing on one's body the fifty letters as the fifty forms of Viṣṇu (Aja, Ānanda, Indra ...) and the parts of the mantras, as part of worship.

equivalents.note: Dvaita's nyāsa places forms of Viṣṇu, not Śākta or Śaiva deities.

name: Mantra repetition (the praṇava and the Viṣṇu mantras)
method_summary: Repetition of the praṇava (for renunciants, who are initiated into it) and of the eight-syllable Nārāyaṇa mantra, the twelve-syllable mantra and others derived from the praṇava, with meditation on the forms they designate.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) into Hari's worship
method_summary: The ācārya initiates a qualified devotee who has undergone the saṃskāras: the disciple sips the Lord's foot-water, receives mantra and vows, and thereafter worships; the Kṛṣṇāmṛtamahārṇava calls those without Hari's initiation 'beasts among men'.
notes: Ritual particulars (maṇḍala, fasting days) deliberately summarized, not listed.

name: Wearing Viṣṇu's heated emblems (tapta-mudrā-dhāraṇa)
method_summary: Summary only: the Mādhva tradition marks the body with Viṣṇu's discus and conch emblems, either heated or in clay; heated emblems are received at set times of the year and at the thread ceremony in the presence of the maṭha's head.
notes: Restricted: involves marking the body with heated metal; no procedure recorded. Its legitimacy was contested by Smārta critics and defended by Mādhva authors (a work 'Cakramīmāṃsā' is ascribed to Vijayīndra) — recalled at low confidence.

name: The upright mark in gopīcandana
method_summary: Marking the forehead (and body) with the upright Vaiṣṇava mark in gopīcandana clay, praised as purifying and required for rites to bear fruit.

name: The daily routine of right conduct (sadācāra)
method_summary: Rising while remembering Hari, purification, cleaning the teeth, sipping water, bathing according to rule, the twilight rites, worship and study, all acts dedicated to Acyuta.

name: Debate for determining the truth (vāda)
method_summary: Debate aimed only at ascertaining the truth, as between teacher and disciple, following the rules of the Kathālakṣaṇa; the maṭhas continue the practice in scholarly disputations.
notes: The maṭha disputations (e.g. during the Cāturmāsya) are recalled, not verified.

name: Recitation of the tradition's hymns
method_summary: Daily recitation of Madhva's Dvādaśastotra and Narasiṃhanakhastuti and Trivikrama's Vāyustuti (framed by the Narasiṃha verses); in the Rāghavendra tradition, the Rāghavendra hymn.

name: The Uḍupi paryāya of Kṛṣṇa worship
method_summary: The worship of the Kṛṣṇa image installed by Madhva at Uḍupi, performed in rotation by the heads of the eight maṭhas, each holding the turn (paryāya) for two years.
notes: The rotation rules are recorded from memory (see lin:udupi-asta-matha).

name: Service at the saints' brindāvanas
method_summary: Worship, circumambulation and vows at the tomb-shrines (brindāvanas) of Mādhva saints — above all Rāghavendra's at Mantrālaya and the Nava Brindāvana near Hampi — where the tradition holds the saints to remain present.
notes: Living practice described from general knowledge; no textual source checked.
